header: Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE); Marcus Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Desai (Aurora Head of ML); Tom Baker (Infra Lead); Javier Morales (Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results, discuss model selection and version pinning strategy, and plan rollbacks/fallbacks.
Covered latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization impact, fallback model routing, and security checklist items.
Agreed next steps: updated benchmarks, security docs, Dedicated pricing call, and new action owners.
transcript: [00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still 45 minutes good?
[00:10] Priya: Yep good for us, we've got an update from the bench team to share as well.
[00:18] Marcus: I dropped the latest perf sheet in the deck link, there's a tab for 1) hosted tests 2) quantized runs and 3) fallback routing tests.
[00:30] Tom: I saw the hosted numbers, looks like median p50 is about 110 ms for the 13B model at seq=64, is that right? The sheet said 112.
[00:42] Marcus: Yeah so that's the Redwood verified run on our hosted infra with batching turned on. p95 is higher around 320ms with the NER prompts.
[00:55] Priya: The issue we hit is with longer invoice prompts, the token length spikes and p95 jumps to 780, so we were discussing pinning to a different model for long-form tasks.

[01:10] Lena: Right — that leads to model selection. We recommended pinning the long-form route to the 20B quantized variant, fallback to 13B where latency sensitive. Also we can do automatic rollbacks if quality regresses.
[01:24] Javier: Can you remind me what 'quantized variant' means here — is data encrypted in memory, and does that affect SOC2?

[01:33] Marcus: Good question, quantization is an execution optimization, it changes numeric precision, not persistence. Encryption at rest and in-transit is still enforced by the platform. We'll share the KMS notes in the security pack.
[01:48] Javier: OK, we need that for our audit. Also want the network diagram showing VPC peering for Private deployment.
[01:56] Lena: We'll include that. Marcus, can you attach the network diagram and KMS note to the shared folder?
[02:04] Marcus: Yep I'll upload after the call.

[02:12] Priya: Back to model pinning — we tried pinning the default route to the 13B for cost reasons but the hallucination rate on our payments prompts was up by 3x compared to the 20B. So there's a clear quality delta.

[02:28] Lena: That's expected. Our recommendation: set the default to 13B for short/interactive UIs, and create a dedicated route for long inference that pins to 20B-quantized. Use the smart routing policy to fallback to 13B only on capacity constraints.
[02:45] Tom: How do rollbacks work? If the 20B rollout has a quality regression after a model update, can we automatically revert to the previous pinned version?

[02:54] Marcus: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback rules. You can configure metric thresholds — e.g., if rouge/accuracy drops by >5% or latency >200ms we flip back. The rollback can be immediate or gradual.
[03:08] Priya: We don't have automatic evals in place for payments-specific quality, can we tie a custom eval set?
[03:15] Marcus: Absolutely, you can upload a prompt set and expected outputs; Redwood Optimize will run quality checks and alert on regressions. We'll show you how to wire that up.
[03:26] Speaker 1: there's also the option to use prefix caching for repeated user contexts, that reduced token cost by about 12% in tests.
[03:36] Lena: Right — caching + batching is the main lever for lowering unit cost while keeping latencies acceptable.
[03:42] Priya: About quantization — we saw the 20B-8bit run had slightly higher tokenization artifacts in the fine-grained NER fields. Is that normal?

[03:51] Marcus: 8-bit quant can slightly impact generation for some edge cases. We have a middle ground: 16-bit hybrid or per-layer quant profiles. For payments NER I'd recommend trying a 16-bit mixed quant first.
[04:05] Tom: From infra perspective, Dedicated will let us pin GPUs and get predictable throughput. Do you have rough pricing?

[04:12] Lena: I'll send the Dedicated pricing sheet after this call — initial commit tiers, burst options, and SLA for p99 latency. Plan for a pilot commit that covers our expected QPS and a short-term burst window.
[04:25] Priya: Our timeline is end of Q2 for pilot completion, and decision by mid-July. So we'll need benchmarks and compliance docs in the next two weeks.
[04:33] Lena: That aligns — we'll prioritize the SOC2 + KMS docs and the benchmark reruns Marcus mentioned.

[04:40] Marcus: I'm going to re-run the latency tests with avg seq=128 and the perf flags we discussed, also include the fallback routing scenario where 20B is full and it routes to 13B. Expect a note in the sheet.
[04:54] Priya: Great. Also we saw a weird tokenization mismatch in the 13B for certain merchant IDs — might be noise but I'll include the examples in the prompt set.
[05:04] Marcus: Cool — please add those to the shared prompt set tab.
[05:10] Javier: On security, small ask — can Redwood provide a sample audit log extract showing RBAC events and model pin changes?
[05:18] Lena: Yes, we can provide a redacted extract. We'll also show how audit logs look in the console and how to export them to your SIEM.
[05:27] Tom: For private deployment, do we need to be on Dedicated first or can the Private control plane be provisioned for pilot?
[05:34] Marcus: We can provision a Private control plane while you run a hosted pilot. Networking is the main lift — VPC peering or private link. We'll provide a network checklist.
[05:44] Priya: A question on fallback logic: if the fallback model produces different output structure, how do we keep downstream parsers from failing?

[05:53] Lena: Two strategies: 1) enforce structured output with function-calling/structured schema so model variants must adhere to shape, 2) include a post-validate step that rejects non-conforming outputs and triggers a retry with the other variant.
[06:08] Priya: We'll probably need both. Our downstream payment parsers are brittle.
[06:12] Marcus: Also the console supports schema validation hooks and we can surfacing those validation failures as metrics for rollbacks.
[06:21] Speaker 2: quick interjection — competitors like Bedrock also have fallback but their observability was weaker in our experience.
[06:29] Lena: Good note; we'll highlight our tracing and token-level cost breakdown in the security pack.
[06:36] Priya: About cost — can you show a modeled per-10k-requests cost for the mixed routing (70% 13B, 30% 20B)?

[06:45] Marcus: I have a simple calc in the sheet. Roughly, mixed routing increases cost by ~35% versus pure 13B but reduces contention and hallucinations by half. I'll add a clearer breakdown by tokens and per-route.
[06:58] Tom: When you talk about auto-scaling on Dedicated, how fast are bursts accommodated? We need to support sudden spike from batch jobs.
[07:06] Marcus: Burst capacity is configurable; typical cold-start to scale within 60-90s depending on GPU warmup. For very fast bursts we recommend keeping a small always-on reserved pool.
[07:16] Priya: For our pilot, we will need a 24/7 ingestion flow — any constraints on KV cache sizes? We store per-customer prefixes to speed up history lookups.
[07:26] Marcus: KV cache sizes are tunable; for Dedicated you control allocation per pool. We'll include recommended settings for a multi-tenant keyspace like yours.
[07:36] Javier: One more security ask: proof of deletion for request logs after retention TTL. Can you confirm we can configure retention per-route?
[07:44] Lena: Yes retention is configurable per-project and per-route, and we can show deletion proof examples in the docs.
[07:52] Priya: Anything else from Redwood before we jump to next steps?

[07:58] Marcus: I'll summarize: re-run latency tests with seq=128 and perf flags, add per-route cost breakdown, attach network diagram and KMS note, and enable a demo of auto-rollback rules next call.
[08:12] Priya: That sounds good. We'll get the prompt set and failing examples to you by Friday.
[08:18] Lena: Perfect. Let's capture action owners then recap timeline. Marcus — run benchmarks by Saturday the 28th; Priya — prompt set by Friday; Lena — pricing and compliance docs by end of week.
[08:30] Tom: Do we want to schedule the Dedicated pricing call now for week of Apr 5?
[08:35] Lena: I'll propose times in calendar; aim for Apr 6 or 7.
[08:40] Javier: One tiny note — the demo for rollbacks, can that be a dry-run not touching prod pinned routes? We prefer a staging only operation.
[08:47] Marcus: Absolutely, we can demo rollout rules in staging with synthetic traffic and show the alerting pipeline.
[08:54] Priya: Ok thanks everyone.
[09:00] Lena: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the bundle: updated sheet, security pack, and pricing. Meeting adjourned.
